questionText: If $\begin{bmatrix}x & 1\end{bmatrix}\begin{bmatrix}1 & 0 \\ -2 & -3\end{bmatrix}\begin{bmatrix}x \\ 2\end{bmatrix} = O$, then the values of $x$ are:

options.mistakeAnalysis: Incorrect option. Inverts the governing property or boundary condition.
Correct answer. Accurately solves the problem for Matrix Multiplication and Equality.
Incorrect option. Applies an adjacent or reciprocal mathematical relation.
Incorrect option. Confuses related NCERT concepts or attributes.

detailedSolution:
Detailed Solution:
For Matrix Multiplication and Equality (Algebra (Matrices and Determinants)):
First compute the product of the first two matrices:
$\begin{bmatrix}x & 1\end{bmatrix}\begin{bmatrix}1 & 0 \\ -2 & -3\end{bmatrix} = \begin{bmatrix}x(1) + 1(-2) & x(0) + 1(-3)\end{bmatrix} = \begin{bmatrix}x - 2 & -3\end{bmatrix}$.
Now multiply by the column vector:
$\begin{bmatrix}x - 2 & -3\end{bmatrix}\begin{bmatrix}x \\ 2\end{bmatrix} = [(x - 2)x + (-3)(2)] = [x^2 - 2x - 6]$.
Equating to the zero matrix $[0]$:
$x^2 - 2x - 6 = 0$.
Using the quadratic formula:
$x = \frac{-(-2) \pm \sqrt{(-2)^2 - 4(1)(-6)}}{2(1)} = \frac{2 \pm \sqrt{4 + 24}}{2} = \frac{2 \pm \sqrt{28}}{2} = \frac{2 \pm 2\sqrt{7}}{2} = 1 \pm \sqrt{7}$.

Therefore, option (B) is the correct answer.

questionText: The system of homogeneous equations $x + ky + 3z = 0$, $3x + ky - 2z = 0$, $2x + 4y - 3z = 0$ has a non-trivial solution if $k$ is equal to:

options.mistakeAnalysis: Incorrect option. Inverts the governing property or boundary condition.
Incorrect option. Applies an adjacent or reciprocal mathematical relation.
Incorrect option. Confuses related NCERT concepts or attributes.
Correct answer. Accurately solves the problem for Homogeneous System of Linear Equations.

detailedSolution:
Detailed Solution:
For Homogeneous System of Linear Equations (Algebra (Matrices and Determinants)):
A system of homogeneous linear equations has a non-trivial solution if and only if the determinant of its coefficient matrix is zero:
$\begin{vmatrix}1 & k & 3 \\ 3 & k & -2 \\ 2 & 4 & -3\end{vmatrix} = 0$
Expand along Row 1:
$1(-3k - (-8)) - k(-9 - (-4)) + 3(12 - 2k) = 0$
$1(-3k + 8) - k(-5) + 3(12 - 2k) = 0$
$-3k + 8 + 5k + 36 - 6k = 0$
$(-3k + 5k - 6k) + (8 + 36) = 0$
$-4k + 44 = 0 \implies 4k = 44 \implies k = 11$.

Therefore, option (D) is the correct answer.

detailedSolution:
Detailed Solution:
For Matrix Inversion and Matrix Equations (Algebra (Matrices and Determinants)):
Let $P = \begin{bmatrix}3 & 1 \\ 2 & 1\end{bmatrix}$, $Q = \begin{bmatrix}2 & 1 \\ 1 & 1\end{bmatrix}$, and $B = \begin{bmatrix}1 & 1 \\ 0 & 1\end{bmatrix}$.
Then $P A Q = B \implies A = P^{-1} B Q^{-1}$.
$\det(P) = 3(1) - 1(2) = 1 \implies P^{-1} = \begin{bmatrix}1 & -1 \\ -2 & 3\end{bmatrix}$.
$\det(Q) = 2(1) - 1(1) = 1 \implies Q^{-1} = \begin{bmatrix}1 & -1 \\ -1 & 2\end{bmatrix}$.
Now compute $P^{-1} B$:
$P^{-1} B = \begin{bmatrix}1 & -1 \\ -2 & 3\end{bmatrix} \begin{bmatrix}1 & 1 \\ 0 & 1\end{bmatrix} = \begin{bmatrix}1(1)+(-1)(0) & 1(1)+(-1)(1) \\ -2(1)+3(0) & -2(1)+3(1)\end{bmatrix} = \begin{bmatrix}1 & 0 \\ -2 & 1\end{bmatrix}$.
Now multiply by $Q^{-1}$:
$A = (P^{-1} B) Q^{-1} = \begin{bmatrix}1 & 0 \\ -2 & 1\end{bmatrix} \begin{bmatrix}1 & -1 \\ -1 & 2\end{bmatrix} = \begin{bmatrix}1(1)+0(-1) & 1(-1)+0(2) \\ -2(1)+1(-1) & -2(-1)+1(2)\end{bmatrix} = \begin{bmatrix}1 & -1 \\ -3 & 4\end{bmatrix}$.

Therefore, option (A) is the correct answer.
